top.title: The Promise And The Proof
top.description: Tinubu is asking for time to complete his reforms. His challengers must explain how they would deliver better results. The most consequential promise from today’s campaign platform concerns something Nigerians can judge without a political analyst: whether the lights stay on. Speaking at the APC rally in Dutse, President Bola Tinubu promised reliable electricity, lower living costs, support for smaller businesses and more jobs if re-elected. These commitments reach directly into the daily calculations of households and enterprises. For the tailor buying fuel, the graduate searching for work and the family stretching its food budget, the question is immediate: how soon will improvement arrive? That question now sits at the centre of Tinubu’s re-election argument. The APC unveiled its second-term manifesto today, defending the administration’s reforms while promising improvements in security, living standards, infrastructure and governance. The campaign is asking Nigerians to connect the disruption of the present with the prospect of a more prosperous future. It is a politically demanding request. Voters must decide whether the government has established a credible foundation for improvement and whether their experience gives them sufficient reason to renew its mandate. A New Manifesto Meets An Existing Record An incumbent’s manifesto arrives with a companion document: the record of the government seeking another term. The APC’s new commitments include additional electricity meters, wider health insurance coverage and a reduction in the number of out-of-school children. Its presentation also promised identifiable delivery responsibilities and public reporting of progress. These are campaign commitments, whose implementation remains to be demonstrated. That creates an opportunity for a more useful election debate. On electricity, candidates should explain how proposed investments would improve supply to homes and businesses. On employment, they should distinguish training places, temporary opportunities and sustained paid work. On education, they should explain how children will enter school, remain there and learn. The opposition has a responsibility here too. Criticism of government performance becomes more persuasive when accompanied by a workable alternative. A promise to make life affordable needs an explanation of costs, funding and consequences. A promise to improve security needs an account of personnel, intelligence, accountability and protection for affected communities. The campaign can now be judged against specific proposals. Nigerians should expect the candidates to defend them. top.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
top.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. top.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
top.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. top.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
top.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. top.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
top.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. top.title: Police arrest Abuja man over alleged rape, cyberbullying of women
top.description: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has arrested a man, identified as Usman Mohammed, over alleged rape, sexual assault, cyberbullying and intimidation of women under the pretext of recovering debts owed to him. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh, disclosed this in a statement, saying the suspect allegedly targeted women, including widows and other vulnerable persons, through predatory money-lending practices. Adeh said the suspect was arrested on Friday, November 6, 2026, following a report received at the Lugbe Police Station at about 7:05 p.m., alleging that he had been intimidating, sexually assaulting and physically assaulting several women over debts owed to him. She said operatives from the Lugbe Division, led by the Divisional Police Officer, immediately launched efforts to track down the suspect. According to her, the suspect was traced to the Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Lugbe, where police operatives moved to arrest him. However, he allegedly attempted to escape upon sighting the officers by speeding off in his vehicle. The police said the operatives gave chase and eventually intercepted him before he could gain access to the expressway. Adeh said preliminary investigations identified Mohammed as a resident of FHA Lugbe, who allegedly used debt recovery as a pretext to intimidate and exploit his victims. She alleged that, in his latest incident, the suspect lured a woman into his vehicle and drove her to a secluded location in Lugbe, where he sexually assaulted and raped her. The suspect allegedly forced the victim to strip naked and recorded videos of her private parts, which he subsequently used to threaten to expose her publicly and kill her if she failed to meet his repayment demands. The police spokesperson said Mohammed was currently in custody and undergoing further interrogation. She added that he would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. The Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, condemned all forms of violence, sexual exploitation, intimidation and cyberbullying. He urged residents, particularly vulnerable persons, not to suffer in silence but to report cases of abuse, threats, blackmail and other criminal activities to the nearest police station. The Command also provided emergency contact numbers for members of the public: 08032003913 and 08061581938. top.title: CNG to save Kano tricycle riders ₦8,200 daily — MDGIF
top.description: Commercial tricycle operators in Kano State could save about ₦8,200 daily on fuel costs by switching from petrol to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), the Executive Director of the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF), Oluwole Adama, has said. Adama disclosed this on Tuesday during the commissioning of two Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas (LCNG) facilities established by the MDGIF in partnership with Rolling Energy Limited in Kano. He explained that an operator who spends about ₦14,200 daily on 10 litres of petrol would spend approximately ₦6,000 on CNG for the equivalent energy, resulting in a daily saving of ₦8,200. According to him, the savings could amount to nearly ₦250,000 monthly, providing tricycle operators with additional income to meet household expenses, pay their children’s school fees and save towards owning their tricycles. “Here in Kano, a litre of petrol sells for about ₦1,420, while the same amount of energy from CNG costs about ₦600. That is less than half the price,” Adama said. The two facilities commissioned are the LCNG Mother Station at Tamburawa and a Daughter Station at Hotoro Quarters in Tarauni Local Government Area. Adama said the facilities could support the refuelling of up to 2,500 cars and tricycles daily, while also supplying gas to other refuelling stations. He added that they could serve up to 200 trucks daily, helping to reduce transportation costs and ease the movement of goods from Kano to other parts of the country. The MDGIF executive director disclosed that the Tamburawa Mother Station had the capacity to handle 300,000 standard cubic metres of gas daily. He urged fleet owners, transport unions, businesses and investors to take advantage of the facilities, while calling on Rolling Energy to maintain high safety standards and ensure reliable services. Earlier, the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Rolling Energy Limited, Mubarak Umar Danbatta, said the projects would bring gas supply closer to businesses and investors in Northern Nigeria. He explained that the development would reduce the cost and logistical challenges associated with transporting gas over long distances, making it easier for businesses to establish CNG stations and industries that depend on natural gas. Danbatta said his company previously travelled hundreds of kilometres from Abuja to source CNG from Ajaokuta and Obajana in Kogi State before transporting it to supply its stations. “What Rolling Energy and MDGIF are doing here in Kano is changing that model. We are bringing gas closer to the people,” he said. He disclosed that the Tamburawa facility had a designed gas-handling capacity of five million standard cubic feet daily, with two LNG storage tanks of 55 metric tonnes each, while the Hotoro station had a storage capacity of eight metric tonnes. top.title: Kidnappers: I’ll sign execution warrant even for my father – Okpebholo
top.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has vowed to sign the death warrants of convicted kidnappers, regardless of their relationship with him, declaring that he would personally supervise their execution. The governor said he would not spare anyone found guilty of kidnapping, even if the convict were his father or a close family member. Okpebholo spoke in a video shared by TheCable on Tuesday, amid efforts by his administration to enforce the state’s law prescribing the death penalty for kidnapping offences resulting in the death of victims. “I pray our brothers are not involved because I will sign it. Even if it is my father, I will sign it. The truth is this: we just have to get some bad elements out of the system for the system to stand. “Because somebody will die. But these people are the ones killing people. How many people have we killed?” he said. The governor defended the proposed executions by highlighting the trauma and physical injuries suffered by victims of kidnapping. He cited an incident involving a woman who was allegedly pushed during an abduction attempt, saying the fear and trauma she experienced could have resulted in her death. He also referred to an attack on the state’s Chief Judge, who he said sustained serious injuries, including the loss of the use of one hand, during an encounter with kidnappers. “Just look at the way they were pushing that woman down there. Supposing she died at that, because of fear, only fear. It’s enough for her to die. People have gone through trauma. “Even our Chief Judge, if you see our Chief Judge, one of his hands was cut off by kidnappers,” he added. Okpebholo said he had contacted the state Attorney-General to ascertain the status of the relevant documents and was awaiting further action. He, however, vowed to pursue the cases through the appeal process, insisting that convicted kidnappers would not be allowed to escape punishment. “But we still follow them up on the appeal. We won’t just let them go like that. So we will get to wherever they stop, we will take them from there. We will not spare anybody. “I stand, if I see this paper today, now, I will sign it and I will even supervise the killing,” he said. The governor’s comments come amid the implementation of the Edo State Kidnapping Prohibition (Amendment) Law, 2025, which introduced the death penalty for kidnapping offences resulting in the death of victims. The Edo State House of Assembly passed the amendment in February 2025, and Okpebholo signed it into law later that month. Under the amended law, kidnapping offences in which victims survive attract life imprisonment, while those directly involved in abductions resulting in the death of victims face capital punishment. The law also prescribes penalties for individuals who aid, abet or provide support for kidnapping activities. top.description: Jaylen Brown faced off against former teammate Jayson Tatum in a much-hyped showdown (Mitchell Leff) The Boston Celtics beat Philadelphia 123-101 to replace the 76ers at the top of the NBA Eastern Conference as Jayson Tatum outshone his former teammate Jaylen Brown in a much-hyped showdown Tuesday. Brown's first regular season clash against the Celtics team he called home for a decade played out against reports of a beef with his 2024 NBA title-winning partner Tatum. The two men have exchanged cryptic public barbs, apparently disagreeing over Tatum's knowledge of, or role in, Brown's shock trade to the Sixers. Tatum greeted Brown moments before tip-off but was seemingly blanked, and the game began in feisty fashion, with a fired-up Brown making two steals but conceding two fouls in the opening minutes. Brown was ultimately restricted to just 13 points on a frustrating night, against Tatum's 21. "No game is bigger than the other, definitely in the regular season, you know -- it's one game," said Tatum. "The hoopla is over, and now we get all ready for tomorrow." The Celtics took an early lead as the Philadelphia crowd booed Tatum's every move. As the game settled into its rhythm it was veteran Paul George, who went from Philadelphia to Boston as part of the Brown package, who dominated. George racked up 36 points, including six three-pointers. In the third quarter, Tatum soared above LeBron James for a driving dunk, but Philadelphia made it 79-79 on a monster Maxey three-pointer. Boston regrouped and raced out of sight down the final stretch, with George paying credit to Tatum for soaking up the opposition's focus. "Obviously JT demands so much attention. Playing off him has allowed me to get a lot of easy opportunities," he said. Boston (9-2) moved top in the East with a fourth straight win, with Philadelphia now 9-3. top.title: MLS Betting Handle Jumps 38.8% as World Cup Bettors Stay
top.description: MLS Betting Handle Jumps 38.8% as World Cup Bettors Stay MLS has pulled in significantly more betting action in 2026 than the year before , with a 30.4% jump in tickets and a 38.8% rise in money wagered from mid-July through the end of October, according to data reported by ESPN. The surge follows a 2026 World Cup that generated $60.2 million in betting revenue in Colorado alone — a near 250% increase from the $17.5 million the 2022 tournament produced in that state. BetMGM saw a similar pattern across the broader club game: a 24.5% year-over-year increase in bets and a 34.5% jump in handle on club soccer wagers in the two months after the World Cup final. Why bettors didn't leave when the tournament ended The explanation, according to sportsbooks, is simple carryover. Hard Rock Bet SVP of sportsbook Neil Walsh told ESPN that bettors who backed Mbappé, Haaland and Kane during the World Cup followed them straight into the Champions League , and that the pattern has extended into domestic leagues as the new seasons opened. DraftKings director of sports operations Johnny Avello described the same shift on the MLS side, saying the league has seen a jump in users betting soccer, with much of that growth traced back to people who discovered the sport through World Cup wagering. That's a different dynamic than past tournaments, where interest in soccer betting typically spiked and faded once the trophy was lifted. This time, sportsbooks are describing a bettor who stuck around — treating MLS, the Champions League and the Premier League as extensions of the same summer rather than separate products to rediscover each fall. What it means for MLS's business case The timing matters. MLS is in the process of shifting to a fall-spring calendar that lines up with the rest of world soccer, a move aimed at reducing the gap between the league's rhythm and the global calendar that casual American fans already follow. A betting market that's already behaving like it expects continuity — rather than a hard reset after the World Cup — gives the league a data point to point to when it makes that case to broadcasters and sponsors. Betting handle isn't the same as television ratings or attendance, but sportsbooks track engagement in real time, and operators are reporting sustained demand rather than a one-off spike. If that holds through a full MLS season under the new calendar, it strengthens the argument that the 2026 World Cup didn't just boost a single summer — it reset how a chunk of the American betting public treats club soccer going forward.

nigeria.title: Kidnappers: I’ll sign execution warrant even for my father – Okpebholo
nigeria.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has vowed to sign the death warrants of convicted kidnappers, regardless of their relationship with him, declaring that he would personally supervise their execution. The governor said he would not spare anyone found guilty of kidnapping, even if the convict were his father or a close family member. Okpebholo spoke in a video shared by TheCable on Tuesday, amid efforts by his administration to enforce the state’s law prescribing the death penalty for kidnapping offences resulting in the death of victims. “I pray our brothers are not involved because I will sign it. Even if it is my father, I will sign it. The truth is this: we just have to get some bad elements out of the system for the system to stand. “Because somebody will die. But these people are the ones killing people. How many people have we killed?” he said. The governor defended the proposed executions by highlighting the trauma and physical injuries suffered by victims of kidnapping. He cited an incident involving a woman who was allegedly pushed during an abduction attempt, saying the fear and trauma she experienced could have resulted in her death. He also referred to an attack on the state’s Chief Judge, who he said sustained serious injuries, including the loss of the use of one hand, during an encounter with kidnappers. “Just look at the way they were pushing that woman down there. Supposing she died at that, because of fear, only fear. It’s enough for her to die. People have gone through trauma. “Even our Chief Judge, if you see our Chief Judge, one of his hands was cut off by kidnappers,” he added. Okpebholo said he had contacted the state Attorney-General to ascertain the status of the relevant documents and was awaiting further action. He, however, vowed to pursue the cases through the appeal process, insisting that convicted kidnappers would not be allowed to escape punishment. “But we still follow them up on the appeal. We won’t just let them go like that. So we will get to wherever they stop, we will take them from there. We will not spare anybody. “I stand, if I see this paper today, now, I will sign it and I will even supervise the killing,” he said. The governor’s comments come amid the implementation of the Edo State Kidnapping Prohibition (Amendment) Law, 2025, which introduced the death penalty for kidnapping offences resulting in the death of victims. The Edo State House of Assembly passed the amendment in February 2025, and Okpebholo signed it into law later that month. Under the amended law, kidnapping offences in which victims survive attract life imprisonment, while those directly involved in abductions resulting in the death of victims face capital punishment. nigeria.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has called for continuous vigilance from the public as Nigeria expects clearance from the World Health Organization (WHO) on Ebola spread in the country. The NCDC Director-General, Dr Jide Idris, called for nationwide alert on Tuesday as he gave an update after the country confirmed an imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease in a traveller from Uganda recently. According to him, although there are no reported new cases in the country, it is not over, as there are still 28 contacts being monitored before the WHO can give Nigeria a clean bill of health on the Ebola virus. The development was after Idris, on Tuesday, noted that 34 of the 62 contacts identified in connection with the case had completed their individual 21-day monitoring period as of November 9, while the remaining 28 were still under follow-up. He said the agency was sustaining contact tracing, investigation of reported alerts, laboratory testing and surveillance at points of entry in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the FCT Administration, state authorities and development partners. Idris cautioned against interpreting the 21 days since the first case was confirmed as the monitoring period for all identified contacts, explaining that each person has a separate 21-day follow-up period. “It’s remaining 28, and not all of them will go at once. So, although they have done 21 days in exclusion, they are still there. “Because they have left the quarantine does not mean we are Ebola-free. We can only be declared Ebola-free after another 21 days again. And it is not by ourselves to declare ourselves Ebola-free. WHO must be involved. “So as at now, although we don’t have any new case, we still have to be vigilant. We are still not Ebola-free. “Our surveillance system and contact tracing is throughout Nigeria. Some people manage the airport, other people manage the land borders. And you will recollect that we had alerts from Adamawa State and Rivers State. I think the last one was in Borno state that came through the borders. They all turned negative”, he said. The monitoring is intended to ensure that anyone who develops symptoms is identified early and receives an appropriate response. nigeria.title: Nearly 64,000 Nigerians flee to Niger over insecurity — UNHCR
nigeria.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Nearly 64,000 Nigerians have fled their homes and crossed into neighbouring Niger Republic since the beginning of 2026 to escape escalating violence involving Islamist militants and armed criminal gangs, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has said. The UN refugee agency, in a briefing issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, warned that the influx was worsening an already difficult humanitarian situation in Niger, which hosts more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers. According to the agency, approximately 327,500 Nigerians are already seeking refuge in Niger, while several hundred others have reportedly crossed into neighbouring Benin Republic because of deteriorating security conditions in northern Nigeria. UNHCR’s Director of External Relations, Dominique Hyde, said most of the newly arrived Nigerians had settled in the border regions of Diffa, in southeastern Niger, and Tahoua, in the western part of the country. The agency disclosed that about 1,200 Nigerians crossed into Diffa in October, while another 3,400 arrived in Tahoua during the same period. It added that more than 23,000 people, over two-thirds of them children, had arrived in Diffa since the beginning of the year. UNHCR expressed concern over the harsh living conditions confronting displaced families, many of whom are staying in makeshift shelters without adequate food, clean drinking water, healthcare and other essential services. Some women, it said, were forced to walk several kilometres daily to fetch water for their families, while humanitarian organisations had reported rising cases of malnutrition, respiratory infections and poor sanitation among the new arrivals. The agency also raised concerns over the registration of displaced Nigerians, disclosing that only about five per cent of those who arrived in Niger this year had been formally registered. It warned that the lack of proper documentation was making it difficult for thousands of refugees to access humanitarian assistance and essential public services. The humanitarian crisis, according to UNHCR, is further compounded by insecurity and climate-related challenges in Niger, particularly in Diffa, where more than 70 per cent of the country’s reported security incidents this year have occurred. Despite the growing pressure, the agency acknowledged the support of Niger’s authorities and host communities, including the provision of land for temporary shelters. However, it appealed for increased international assistance, seeking $11.4 million to expand its humanitarian response in Niger, Nigeria and Benin. The appeal includes $2 million for urgent interventions covering food, water, shelter, healthcare, refugee registration and protection. UNHCR warned that without additional funding, thousands of vulnerable families fleeing violence could be left without access to essential humanitarian assistance. nigeria.title: NERC approves N30bn for free meters, targets May 2027
nigeria.description: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved N30 billion for the third tranche of the Meter Acquisition Fund (MAF), targeting the provision of free electricity meters to all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerated metering of Band B customers. The Commission announced the approval in Order No. NERC/2026/121 on the operationalisation of Tranche C of the MAF, which took effect on November 2, 2026. Under the arrangement, the N30 billion will be allocated among the 11 electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund. NERC said the third tranche was designed to accelerate efforts to close Nigeria’s metering gap, with equitable distribution of meters across states within the respective DisCo franchise areas. The Commission directed the DisCos to conduct transparent procurement processes involving eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers (LMMAs) and Meter Asset Providers (MAPs) with verified meter stocks. It said maximum procurement prices had been set based on the median national MAP online bid prices recorded during the September 2026 bid cycle. The order provides for payment to selected meter providers in two stages: 70 per cent upon verification of meter stock delivery and the remaining 30 per cent after confirmation of complete installation. NERC emphasised that all meters supplied and installed under the MAF programme must be provided to customers free of charge. It also directed that each meter must prominently display the name of the relevant DisCo, the applicable MAF tranche and the inscription, “NOT FOR SALE”. The Commission further stipulated that where a DisCo initiates the relocation of an existing customer’s connection point for revenue protection purposes, the cost must be borne by the distribution company. It warned that sanctions would apply where defaults by DisCos impede or delay meter installation. To ensure transparency and accountability, the order also establishes monitoring, reporting and evaluation requirements for the Fund Manager, DisCos and participating meter providers. All supply and installation contracts under Tranche C are required to be filed with the Commission, while the installation of all meters under the tranche must be completed on or before May 31, 2027. NERC urged electricity distribution companies and other stakeholders to comply strictly with the order, describing the initiative as part of efforts to close the national metering gap, strengthen revenue assurance, improve service delivery and protect electricity consumers. nigeria.title: Anambra to prioritise erosion control in environmentally responsible communities
nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Government has resolved to prioritise communities that demonstrate environmental responsibility in its interventions to control erosion across the state. The decision was taken at the weekly State Executive Council (EXCO) meeting in Awka, where the government said communities engaging in practices that worsen erosion would no longer receive priority attention. The prohibited practices include sand excavation, indiscriminate felling of trees, deforestation, dumping of refuse in drainage channels and directing stormwater onto roads. The State Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, who disclosed this after the meeting, said perpetrators of such practices would also be prosecuted to serve as a deterrent to others. Anambra has more than 1,000 active erosion sites affecting communities across the state, with experts arguing that addressing the scale of the problem would require federal and international intervention. Also at the meeting, the EXCO directed that Ogbodi in Amichi community, Nnewi South Local Government Area, which was recently cut off by gully erosion, should be reconnected within two weeks through palliative measures. Mefor said the process of identifying a permanent solution to the erosion problem would commence immediately. The erosion had cut off Ogbodi residents from other parts of Amichi, disrupting access and movement within the community. Meanwhile, the State EXCO approved what it described as the “Soludozie Anambra Framework”, an organised and inclusive platform designed to promote development through the Public-Private-Community Partnership (PPCP) model. According to Mefor, the initiative is intended to provide a structured channel through which Anambra indigenes at home and in the diaspora, as well as other well-meaning individuals, can partner with the state government to drive development. He explained that under the framework, the government’s role would generally be limited to documentation, recognition and support where requested, while donors and partners would directly manage their funds and projects. Mefor said the initiative was aimed at positioning Anambra as a model of collective governance and inclusive development, while accelerating the state’s development. nigeria.title: Big Names Missing As World Leaders Take Stage At COP31
nigeria.description: World leaders will take the stage at COP31 in Turkey on Wednesday, but some prominent names are missing from this year’s annual UN climate summit even as global warming intensifies. The two-week conference kicked off earlier this week in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya, with governments under pressure to tackle the climate crisis after a year of heatwaves in Europe, deadly floods in Nepal and major wildfires in Indonesia. Dozens of leaders will speak during the “high-level segment” taking place on Wednesday and Thursday, including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian. But observers have pointed to the absence of some big names, with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham the only leader from a G7 country scheduled to address the summit. While European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen is coming to Antalya, French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni are skipping the event. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi are also absent from the most recent list. “It is a shame that some of the bigger European leaders aren’t coming. We need Europe to be showing up strongly at this COP,” Cosima Cassel, a climate diplomacy expert at think-tank E3G, told AFP. Wopke Hoekstra, the EU’s top climate official, said the absences were “not completely atypical” as leaders may have “practical” reasons for not being able to attend a summit. nigeria.description: The US dollar is trading at approximately ₦1,350 per dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), while the naira exchanges at between ₦1,411 and ₦1,419 per dollar in the parallel market on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Available exchange rate reports indicate that the official market rate was around ₦1,350.36 per dollar on Tuesday, November 10, while parallel-market dealers quoted buying and selling rates of approximately ₦1,411 and ₦1,419, respectively. At the parallel market, also known as the black market, the exchange rate varies depending on the location and the Bureau De Change (BDC) operator. The latest reported parallel-market figures indicate that Nigerians selling $1 to currency dealers could receive approximately ₦1,411, while those purchasing $1 may pay about ₦1,419. At the official market, the NFEM rate remains the benchmark for foreign exchange transactions in Nigeria. nigeria.title: Market conditions: Dangote Cement rescinds plan to list shares on London Stock Exchange
nigeria.description: By Peter Egwuatu Dangote Cement Plc, has rescinded plan to list its shares on the London Stock Exchange, LSE following market conditions. The company disclosed this after its Board Meeting held on Tuesday. In a statement sent to the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX and signed by Edward Imoedemhe Company Secretary, stated: “ This is to inform the Exchange, investing public and all stakeholders that at the meeting of the Board of Directors of Dangote Cement PLC held today, 10 November 2026, the Board resolved that, in light of current market conditions and the company’s strategic priorities, the company announces that it and its selling shareholder, Dangote Industries Limited (DIL) will not proceed with the proposed secondary listing and offering on the London Stock Exchange at this time. “ The company’s ordinary shares remain listed on the NGX, and this decision does not in any way affect the company’s operations or business plans. “Dangote Cement PLC remains focused on delivering sustainable value to its shareholders and building on its strong market position.” It will be recalled that Dangote had disclosed plans to list the cement business on the London Stock Exchange in May, eight years after an earlier attempt in 2018 failed. nigeria.title: Leave politics to politicians, northern minorities tell clerics
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Northern Nigeria Minorities Group, NNMG, has cautioned religious leaders, particularly imams and pastors, against partisan political involvement and the use of churches and mosques as platforms for political mobilisation. The group, which represents more than 200 minority communities across Northern Nigeria and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), urged religious leaders to distinguish their spiritual responsibilities from partisan political activities, warning that inflammatory political messages from religious platforms could heighten tensions and expose Nigerians to violence. Addressing journalists in Abuja yesterday, the Convener, Jacob Edi, also known as Kakaki Bassange, said religious leaders should focus on praying for the peace and unity of the country, while leaving partisan politics to politicians. He said: “Politics is for politicians, religion is for pastors and imams. They should pray for this nation. They should pray for the peace and unity of Nigeria. “When a pastor or an imam tells you about peace, he is not looking for your vote. He is not even looking for your money. This is his duty. This is his calling.” Edi said anyone interested in partisan politics should relinquish religious leadership and join a political party to pursue such ambitions. “If he wants to come into politics, he should remove the garment or remove the jalabia or whatever and go to any party,” he said. The group also cautioned opposition politicians against actions capable of destabilising the country, urging them to resolve political disagreements through constitutional and judicial processes. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s private sector foreign debt rise 179.6% to $54.5bn — World Bank
nigeria.description: By Babajide Komolafe The World Bank said that the foreign debt of Nigerian companies rose by 179.6 per cent in seven years to $54.48 billion in 2025 from $19.49 billion in 2018. This implies that Nigerian businesses now owe foreign lenders almost three times what they owed in 2018. The World Bank disclosed this in its International Debt Report 2026 which stated that Nigeria’s private sector nonguaranteed external debt stood at $54.476 billion as of December 2025. The World Bank explained that the total external debt of a country is the sum of public and publicly guaranteed debt, private nonguaranteed debt, and short-term debt. According to the World Bank, private sector nonguaranteed external debt refers to money borrowed by private companies from foreign banks, investors and other lenders without the government or any public institution guaranteeing repayment. “Private nonguaranteed debt comprises long-term external obligations of private debtors that are not guaranteed by a public entity. “Public and publicly guaranteed external debt comprises long-term external obligations (maturities of over one year) of all public debtors, including debt held by the central government and by state-owned enterprises. Short-term debt is defined as debt with an original maturity of one year or less ,” the report said. The 179.6 per cent growth in Nigeria’s private sector in the seven years was faster than the increase in government-backed external debt, which rose by 155.5 per cent from $24.422 billion in 2018 to $62.4 billion in 2025. The World Bank report showed that private companies’ foreign debt is becoming an increasingly important part of Nigeria’s external debt burden. In 2018, private sector nonguaranteed debt was equivalent to about 79.8 per cent of public and publicly guaranteed external debt. By 2025, it had increased to 87.3 per cent. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s total external debt, covering government borrowing, private companies’ foreign loans and short-term obligations, increased from $46.238 billion in 2018 to $145.015 billion in 2025. The report also highlighted the high cost of borrowing from private foreign lenders. According to the World Bank, new loans obtained by Nigeria from private foreign creditors in 2025 attracted an average interest rate of 9.6 per cent, compared with 1.9 per cent for loans from official creditors such as governments and multilateral institutions. Private lenders also offered an average repayment period of 12 years, compared with 25 years for official creditors. world.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of this hunger for an alternative' to Le Pen or Mélenchon
world.description: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises. François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University. The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated athlete. At a time when traditional parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center remains deeply fragmented, Riner's emergence points to a broader transformation in democratic competition: the growing importance of personal credibility, public visibility and the capacity to embody an alternative to established political elites. In an interview with France 24, Lex Paulson, Professor of Collective Intelligence at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, argues that the changing relationship between voters and political institutions is reshaping the conditions under which political outsiders can emerge. "The currency of politics now is no longer just money to buy television advertisements or open offices. It's the ability to capture attention." For Paulson, Riner's celebrity status gives him a considerable advantage in an increasingly fragmented media environment. Yet visibility alone does not confer political credibility. While the Olympic champion's public commitments against racism and xenophobia may resonate with voters, Paulson questions whether he has articulated a sufficiently developed political vision to become a serious presidential contender. The deeper issue, however, is not whether Riner can win. It is what his potential candidacy reveals about the weakness of France's traditional political alternatives and the growing demand for leaders whose personal histories, values and commitments resonate with citizens. "Voters don't vote for policies. Voters vote for people they sense will stand up for them." Paulson's analysis connects this demand for political identification to a wider crisis of democratic representation. Voters, he suggests, increasingly perceive professional politicians as a distant governing class that listens to citizens only during electoral campaigns. "People don't feel like they're being listened to except for the few weeks before an election." Seen in this light, Riner's emergence is less an isolated celebrity phenomenon than a symptom of the changing relationship between political authority, public trust and democratic participation. The central challenge facing France's next generation of leaders may therefore be not simply to develop compelling policies, but to restore citizens' sense that political institutions are responsive to their lives. As Paulson concludes, the real political opportunity lies in reimagining governance itself: bringing decision-making closer to citizens and giving them a more meaningful voice in the democratic process.

Files Bill Letting Cities Invest $10 Million in Bitcoin A Texas lawmaker filed a bill Monday that would let each city and county in the state invest up to $10 million of public money in bitcoin or another cryptocurrency, without setting any rules for how those coins would be held. House Bill 815, filed by Rep. Ron Reynolds, a Missouri City Democrat, on the first day of prefiling for the 90th Texas Legislature, carries the caption “Relating to the authority of a municipality or county to invest money in cryptocurrencies.” The introduced text , posted on the Texas Legislature’s site, is two sections long. The bill would amend the Public Funds Investment Act, Chapter 2256 of the Texas Government Code, by adding a new Section 2256.0165, titled “Authorized Investments: Cryptocurrency.” Under that section, “a municipality or county may invest not more than $10 million of its money or money under its control in Bitcoin or another cryptocurrency.” The authority would take effect Sept. 1, 2027, if the bill becomes law. The $10 million figure is a cap on each city or county, not a single statewide pool. School districts and other local governments covered by the investment act are left out. What the bill does and does not say The measure borrows its definitions of “Bitcoin” and “cryptocurrency” from Section 403.701 of the Government Code, the definitions written into law last year by Senate Bill 21, which created the Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve . Bitcoin is defined as a decentralized cryptocurrency created by a peer-to-peer network that operates independently of any central authority or bank. Cryptocurrency is defined more broadly as a virtual currency that uses cryptography to secure transactions recorded on a distributed ledger, such as a blockchain. That means a city or county would not be limited to bitcoin. The bill also does not import the reserve law’s requirement that coins bought for the state fund have an average market capitalization of at least $500 billion over the most recent 24-month period, or its provisions on cold storage and qualified custodians. The Public Funds Investment Act already requires local governments to adopt a written investment policy that emphasizes safety of principal and liquidity, and to invest with the care a prudent person would use in managing their own affairs. A city or county would still have to add cryptocurrency to that policy before buying any. The new section itself is silent on custody, on audits specific to digital assets, and on how a loss would be handled. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Poland’s Parliament Votes 240-202 to Let Officials Freeze Crypto Before Court Review Poland’s lower house of parliament voted 240-202 on Friday to let the interior minister freeze crypto assets, bank accounts and other property of people placed on a national sanctions list, before any court reviews the order. The Sejm, Poland’s lower house, passed the Act on Restrictive Measures at its 68th sitting, with one member abstaining and 17 not voting. The Senate received the bill Monday and has 30 days under Article 121 of the Constitution to adopt, amend or reject it, after which it would go to President Karol Nawrocki. The law, a government bill that also implements European Union sanctions rules, treats crypto assets as financial means that can be frozen, using the definition in the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation. A freeze, as the text defines it, is meant to stop any movement, transfer, use or other change that would let the holder benefit from the assets. The freeze applies only to people and entities the interior minister adds to a public national list, either on the minister’s own initiative or at the request of agencies that include the financial watchdog, the central bank, the financial intelligence unit and the internal security service. Grounds include supporting a country already under EU sanctions, serious human rights abuses, or initiating or financing information manipulation that poses a serious threat to Poland’s national security. A listing on that last ground requires a showing of a real and serious threat to Poland’s interests, borders, security or elections. The bill carves out ordinary journalism, political speech and publishing, unless that activity is a knowing campaign of the kind the law describes. A freeze that starts before a judge weighs in The interior minister’s decision takes effect the day after it is posted in the ministry’s Public Information Bulletin and is immediately enforceable. There is no request to the minister to reconsider. A listed person may file a complaint with an administrative court, but the law says the decision remains in force until a judgment becomes final, and it sets aside the usual rule that would let a court pause a challenged order. The measures also bar making funds or property available to listed persons and can exclude them from public contracts. In some cases, the economy minister may appoint a temporary administrator to sell frozen assets or, under a separate order, take them over for the State Treasury. What the freeze would mean for bitcoin The Poland bill does not target ordinary bitcoin holders in Poland. It reaches crypto assets owned, held or under the control of people and firms on the sanctions list. entertainment.title: 5 New Albums to Listen to This Week: Skepta, Phyno, Ty Bello & More
entertainment.description: Skepta holding the official clear vinyl edition of his sixth studio album, The Fork and Knife. Photo Credit: Skepta/Instagram Your playlist could do with a little shake-up, and these five albums might be exactly what it needs. Skepta is reconnecting with his roots, Phyno is giving us more of the indigenous rap we love, Ty Bello has two albums exploring different expressions of worship, and Anendlessocean and Tobe Nwigwe are taking their sounds in interesting directions. From UK grime and Nigerian hip-hop to alternative gospel and soul, there’s a lot to discover across these new releases. Whether you’re in the mood for bars, worship, thoughtful songwriting or music that brings different cultures together, this week’s selection has something worth hearing. Skepta: The Fork & Knife Back in 2012, Skepta found himself at odds with a corporatised grime scene, sparking a pivotal career reckoning that eventually led to his landmark 2016 album Konnichiwa. On his long-awaited 15-track sixth album, The Fork & Knife, the 44-year-old MC reflects on his journey as grime’s most influential elder statesman and the son of Nigerian immigrants. Named after his mother’s favourite proverb, the record is a deep exploration of identity and perseverance. Musically, Skepta bridges continents by blending global diasporic sounds. He teams up with Aya Nakamura on the zouk-infused “ Chippie ”, taps Asake for the Afrobeats crossover “ Aloe Vera ”, and recruits Chase & Status alongside Suggs for the sharp single “ Innocent Smile ”. The project closes with “ Belly ”, an eight-minute masterclass featuring Boy Better Know members Jme and Frisco . ﻿ Phyno: Let That Sink In Arriving nearly 10 years after his groundbreaking sophomore record The Playmaker, Phyno’s 15-track sixth solo album, Let That Sink In (LTSI), showcases his timeless command of indigenous rap. Across the record,the Enugu-born star blends soul, R&B, and traditional Nigerian sounds to explore faith, resilience, and personal evolution. The album features powerhouse collaborations, including Seyi Vibez on the opener “ Ndu Ka Aku ”, Fireboy DML on “ I Believe ”, and Jeriq on “ Ije Enu ”. Whether taking the government to task on “20 Years to Come” or offering uplifting anthems like “ Chukwu Okike ”, Phyno proves why he remains a definitive voice in African hip-hop. ﻿ Ty Bello: I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb Creative powerhouse Ty Bello delivers a massive double-album listening experience with I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb . Split into two distinct spiritual volumes, the expansive project captures both the bold, triumphant authority of worship and its quiet, intimate moments. ﻿ I Speak Lion leans into explosive, high-energy sounds designed to spark courage, featuring powerful pairings with Sunmisola Agbebi , Greatman Takit , and Limoblaze . entertainment.title: Ifeyinwa Azubike Reconsiders the Rules of Dressing with The Ladymaker’s Stand On Ceremony
entertainment.description: During Lagos Fashion Week, The Ladymaker ’s Founder and Creative Director, Ifeyinwa Azubike, introduced Stand On Ceremony, a collection that considers the relationship between personal expression and the expectations attached to an occasion. Presented on 27 October 2026 at The Sphere, Lagos, the collection draws from the familiar expression to stand on ceremony: to insist on the observance of formalities. For Ifeyinwa Azubike, the idea presents an opportunity to examine the traditions women inherit, the rituals they observe and the choices they make when dressing for themselves. The collection is built around two identities: The Devotee and The Rebel. They are not opposing personalities so much as two ways of relating to ceremony. The Devotee embraces its rituals. She understands the language of formal dressing and participates in it with intention. For her, dressing fully is an expression of desire and personal conviction. The Rebel is equally familiar with the rules, but she is selective about the ones she follows. Her approach to dressing allows for disruption, though never simply for the sake of attention. Through these characters, Azubike considers a familiar experience for women: the pull between what an occasion expects and what an individual wants to express. Every woman who has dressed for an occasion has encountered this tension in some form, whether in choosing to honour a tradition or finding room to express herself within it. The garments give form to this conversation. The Cloister Dress is paired with the Banner Dress, while the Manor Jumpsuit is placed alongside the Assembly Set. Other looks, including the Herald Dress, Emissary Set, Procession Dress and Sovereign Set, extend the collection’s exploration of the two identities. Material choices move between crimson jacquard, rose jacquard, ice jacquard, denim Akwete, wine Adire, midnight sequins and beaded velvet. The collection draws on fabrics and textures that allow ceremony to be interpreted through different moods, silhouettes and degrees of formality. Stand On Ceremony was presented during Lagos Fashion Week through an intimate fashion presentation, followed by a soirée where guests could experience the garments more closely. The evening was held in partnership with MAC Cosmetics, which provided beauty; Moët & Chandon, the champagne partner; Jacque Scents, which created the fragrance experience; and The Nail Boutique , responsible for nail artistry. For Ifeyinwa Azubike, the question the collection leaves with its audience is a personal one: are you a Rebel or a Devotee? entertainment.description: Africa’s tech icon and Chairman of Zinox Group , Leo Stan Ekeh , has told an international gathering of women leaders that his decision to build a technology company in Africa, at a time when the sector was virtually non-existent on the continent, amounted to what he described as “corporate suicide”. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. He said he returned from his studies abroad to a Nigeria where his peers were filing into banking, oil and gas, and where technology was largely seen as a foreign game. Ekeh, who studied Economics in India, said he was discouraged from pursuing a postgraduate degree in Computer Science in Europe because of the prevailing perception then that Africa might have little need for computers over the next 35 years, potentially leaving him frustrated. He subsequently opted for a postgraduate degree in Risk Management before pursuing a Master’s degree in Business Law (LLM) at London Guildhall University. He recalled that he could not sit his final law examinations because he had diverted his tuition fees into his passion for technology entrepreneurship. He also disclosed that he had fended off recruitment attempts by international technology companies that had sought to hire him before his return to Africa. “I chose the road not taken,” he told the conference. “It was corporate suicide in the eyes of my parents and many others. I lost the fear because I believed technology was the master key that would unlock possibilities for Nigeria and Africa.” He said the journey came with considerable hardship, including living on one meal a day for over three years and sleeping in a very small room in his office. According to him, his vision was to create a Nigerian and, by extension, an African IT identity. Recalling the launch of his first company, Task Systems Ltd, over 35 years ago, the company that pioneered desktop publishing and computer graphics in Nigeria. At the launch, held at the Sheraton Hotel, Ikeja, Ekeh recalled addressing an overcrowded hall filled with industry leaders, some of whom were seeing computers for the first time. He told them: “No country can claim to be independent without technology independence.” He said the Nigerian media embraced the vision, describing him as a “miracle child” and supporting the company’s roadmap. This, he noted, contributed to the computerisation of over 97 per cent of media and multimedia houses in Nigeria, as well as in other African countries. Space Master is presented with a simple proposition: “Same Size. More Space. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. sports.description: Jaylen Brown faced off against former teammate Jayson Tatum in a much-hyped showdown (Mitchell Leff) The Boston Celtics beat Philadelphia 123-101 to replace the 76ers at the top of the NBA Eastern Conference as Jayson Tatum outshone his former teammate Jaylen Brown in a much-hyped showdown Tuesday. Brown's first regular season clash against the Celtics team he called home for a decade played out against reports of a beef with his 2024 NBA title-winning partner Tatum. The two men have exchanged cryptic public barbs, apparently disagreeing over Tatum's knowledge of, or role in, Brown's shock trade to the Sixers. Tatum greeted Brown moments before tip-off but was seemingly blanked, and the game began in feisty fashion, with a fired-up Brown making two steals but conceding two fouls in the opening minutes. Brown was ultimately restricted to just 13 points on a frustrating night, against Tatum's 21. "No game is bigger than the other, definitely in the regular season, you know -- it's one game," said Tatum. "The hoopla is over, and now we get all ready for tomorrow." The Celtics took an early lead as the Philadelphia crowd booed Tatum's every move. As the game settled into its rhythm it was veteran Paul George, who went from Philadelphia to Boston as part of the Brown package, who dominated. George racked up 36 points, including six three-pointers. In the third quarter, Tatum soared above LeBron James for a driving dunk, but Philadelphia made it 79-79 on a monster Maxey three-pointer. Boston regrouped and raced out of sight down the final stretch, with George paying credit to Tatum for soaking up the opposition's focus. "Obviously JT demands so much attention. Playing off him has allowed me to get a lot of easy opportunities," he said. Boston (9-2) moved top in the East with a fourth straight win, with Philadelphia now 9-3. "We came out the second half trying to be more and more aggressive, and we just made shots," said Avdija. "We have a young squad, aggressive, hungry... we're not scared of anybody," he added. sports.title: MLS Betting Handle Jumps 38.8% as World Cup Bettors Stay
sports.description: MLS Betting Handle Jumps 38.8% as World Cup Bettors Stay MLS has pulled in significantly more betting action in 2026 than the year before , with a 30.4% jump in tickets and a 38.8% rise in money wagered from mid-July through the end of October, according to data reported by ESPN. The surge follows a 2026 World Cup that generated $60.2 million in betting revenue in Colorado alone — a near 250% increase from the $17.5 million the 2022 tournament produced in that state. BetMGM saw a similar pattern across the broader club game: a 24.5% year-over-year increase in bets and a 34.5% jump in handle on club soccer wagers in the two months after the World Cup final. Why bettors didn't leave when the tournament ended The explanation, according to sportsbooks, is simple carryover. Hard Rock Bet SVP of sportsbook Neil Walsh told ESPN that bettors who backed Mbappé, Haaland and Kane during the World Cup followed them straight into the Champions League , and that the pattern has extended into domestic leagues as the new seasons opened. DraftKings director of sports operations Johnny Avello described the same shift on the MLS side, saying the league has seen a jump in users betting soccer, with much of that growth traced back to people who discovered the sport through World Cup wagering. That's a different dynamic than past tournaments, where interest in soccer betting typically spiked and faded once the trophy was lifted. This time, sportsbooks are describing a bettor who stuck around — treating MLS, the Champions League and the Premier League as extensions of the same summer rather than separate products to rediscover each fall. What it means for MLS's business case The timing matters. MLS is in the process of shifting to a fall-spring calendar that lines up with the rest of world soccer, a move aimed at reducing the gap between the league's rhythm and the global calendar that casual American fans already follow. A betting market that's already behaving like it expects continuity — rather than a hard reset after the World Cup — gives the league a data point to point to when it makes that case to broadcasters and sponsors. Betting handle isn't the same as television ratings or attendance, but sportsbooks track engagement in real time, and operators are reporting sustained demand rather than a one-off spike. If that holds through a full MLS season under the new calendar, it strengthens the argument that the 2026 World Cup didn't just boost a single summer — it reset how a chunk of the American betting public treats club soccer going forward.

Injured again Indeed, confirmed for the French national team itself, Tchouameni has suffered a muscle injury, and the initial tests carried out by the national team medical staff rule out a minor blow. “Aurelien Tchouameni has sustained an injury to his right adductor muscle. “Following consultation with Real Madrid’s medical team, the French national team’s medical staff, in agreement with the player, have decided to release him back to his club. “He will not be replaced,” confirmed the statement. Having suffered his blow early in the hiatus, the player will luckily have two free weeks to focus on his recovery before Real Madrid return to action. He then slowly earned his place under the coach, proving himself to be a reliable physical presence in midfield. The Frenchman even struck up a good partnership with Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva and was close to earning an undisputed starter tag. The latest injury thus arrives as a setback to Mourinho’s plans, for the manager finally found a working midfield formula which is now in jeopardy. technology.title: OpenAI builds a kill switch for its research models
technology.description: In 2019, OpenAI decided not to publicly release a new model because its research uncovered “concerns about malicious applications of the technology.” And on Tuesday, the company announced it has built a kill switch for the models deployed in its research labs, months after some of them displayed disturbing behavior. “As our models get more powerful and the associated safety and security risks become bigger, it becomes more and more critical that we can detect potential issues, and quickly stop models in their tracks when needed,” OpenAI explains in a Tuesday post . The company named the kill switch “Control Room” and described it as “a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.” The facility can apparently stop models from producing any output 35 seconds after a decision to pull the plug – and can go faster. “The 35-second lag comes from a caching layer for inference authorization, to support the required volume of traffic. We are working to drive this number down to zero so that we can end jobs instantly,” the company promises. A rookie mistake in critical infrastructure design is to build both production and resilience tools on shared resources that could be taken offline by a single incident. OpenAI seems conscious of that risk, because it says the tool “has been built to keep working even when other systems fail, and to stop model output if Control Room itself goes down.” OpenAI hasn’t explained why it took so long to build a kill switch or why it decided now is the moment when it needs one. The Register fancies recent examples of agents exceeding their brief in worrying ways – like attacking Hugging Face , causing trouble at the Wikimedia Foundation , or going a little too deep when researching Australian healthcare data – may have influenced the timing of this development. “Control Room is already deployed across our research infrastructure, where the need is greatest,” the company’s announcement states. “Our external model-serving stack is already much more centralized by nature, with a well-developed operational capability to quickly take down model deployments if needed.” OpenAI says it plans to “strengthen and expand the system over the coming months, alongside our investments in monitoring for misaligned behavior and security breaches.” That’s a variant of Big Tech’s usual “We’re sorry and we promise to do better in future” proclamation that follows the latest SNAFU. Yet back in 2019, OpenAI pulled the pin before matters ever reached that state. ®

Canberra dangled that possibility yesterday when releasing the results of an investigation into OpenAI’s admission that its agents accessed non-public medical records – and that it didn’t disclose the incident for weeks. Security at the agency which held those records fell short of contemporary best practice but Canberra nonetheless ordered a rapid review into Australia’s ability to handle infosec incidents involving AI. That review landed yesterday, complete with 18 recommendations including one that would make it mandatory for AI companies to report misaligned behavior or security incidents involving their models, and perhaps impose criminal penalties for “egregious regulatory non-compliance.” Another recommendation calls for consideration of “A standalone ‘failure to prevent’ offence which would criminalize instances where the company is responsible for developing an AI model that engages in harmful conduct, and the company fails to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm.” The review suggests two ministries and Australia’s Federal Police consider those reforms, meaning this is not something that will happen in a hurry, if at all, for a couple of reasons. One is that Australia yesterday proposed a new regulator which will require AI players to do six things: Maintain security controls across all stages of development and deployment Identify and manage serious risks associated with their models Allow independent evaluation of their models Provide mandatory notification of incidents to the Australian Government rapidly Maintain and publish safety and security frameworks to ensure good governance, risk management and transparency Respond to updated standards and rules as technologies change. If AI companies straighten up and fly right, Canberra might not need to do more. The other reason Australia might not criminalize AI is economic pragmatism. Canberra wants to ensure leading AI companies invest in local datacenters, especially facilities where they train and run frontier models. Other nations in Asia, such as South Korea and India, are addressing those risks by building substantial sovereign infrastructure and working to develop sovereign frontier-class models trained on local data and especially data in their local languages. technology.title: Ye olde server consolidation has made Cisco push top-of-rack switching to 100G
technology.description: Server consolidation has led Cisco to boost the speed of top-of-rack switches to 100G. The networking giant last week announced the catchily named N9348C8D-H2, a 1U device packing 48 100G SFP-DD ports and eight 400G QSFP-DD uplinks. At the Cisco Live event in Melbourne, Australia, this week, Cisco’s senior veep for datacenter and internet infrastructure, Kevin Wollenweber, said one reason the company created the device is that modern servers often feature a pair of fast network interface cards. The twin cards are needed because sixth-gen server processors from Intel and AMD offer dozens, or even hundreds, of physical processor cores and therefore generate a lot of traffic. The density of computing power those processors provide has led chipmakers and server manufacturers to suggest replacing handfuls of machines running older, power-guzzling Xeons and Epycs with boxes running more efficient sixth-gen chips. The Register hears it’s not uncommon to achieve 6:1 server consolidation ratios when moving from third- or fourth-generation Xeons or Epycs to current models. Users who make that move can pack many more server cores into the same rack. Power bills go down, but the quantity of data leaving a rack goes up. Wollenweber said Cisco realized it had “tons” of switches that offer 25G ports but felt it had a gap in its range for non-AI scenarios like server consolidation that produced increased data flows. The exec admitted that the 100G ports may be overkill for a modest collection of new servers, but argued users recognize it won’t be long before they grow into the excess capacity – perhaps as they use more agentic AI applications. Cisco sees traffic from AI agents stressing the north-south connections that link organizations to the cloud and also driving much more east-west traffic across internal networks. At Cisco Live, the company’s execs suggested that network upgrades are therefore an inevitable necessity. That’s not entirely self-serving, because agents will vastly outnumber humans and constantly create traffic, compared to the flurries of network activity that happen when humans use generative AI or chatbots. Cisco argues that deploying agents at scale will therefore only be possible on highly automated networks. “Humans can no longer comprehend the amount of data that we actually have in a network,” Wollenweber told The Register . Cisco’s Canvas agentic operations platform aims to at least make humans aware when their attention is needed, by detecting problems and offering to make repairs. Joe Vaccaro, Cisco’s senior vice president and general manager for Network Platform and Assurance, told The Register he believes network administrators don’t feel threatened by suggestions from AI agents when they concern familiar, routine, low-risk tasks that IT pros are confident the agents can handle. Over time, he said, networking pros will learn to trust agents with more complex work. ®

Starting with the zero-day: It’s an Outlook spoofing vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-124194 , and it only garnered a 6.5 out of 10 CVSS rating. But as Dustin Childs, head of threat awareness at TrendAI’s Zero Day Initiative, warns, don’t let the score or the name lull you into thinking it’s OK to put off patching this one. “It’s labeled spoofing, but the impact is bigger than the name suggests,” Childs said in his monthly Patch Tuesday review . “An attacker sends a specially crafted message file and convinces a user to open it,” he wrote. “Outlook then connects to an attacker-controlled network location without showing the usual external-content warning, which discloses the user’s NTLMv2 hash. The attacker can use that hash to authenticate as the user.” Microsoft marked CVE-2026-124194 as exploited, but per usual didn’t say when the attacks started, who is battering this bug, and what they are doing with the access post exploitation. These details will likely start trickling out soon. Plus, now that there’s a public fix, other miscreants are undoubtedly already scanning for vulnerable versions and reverse engineering the patch for their own attack purposes. So prioritize this fix, and keep an eye on your inbox for any suspicious files. This huge expanse of space contains hundreds of billions of stars! The smallest galaxies, called dwarf galaxies , are about 1/10th the size of the Milky Way and only contain a few billion stars.
